chunks: [A part of the same sermon about the Prophet]

Allāh kept the Prophets in deposit in the best place of deposit and made them stay in the best place of stay. He moved them in succession from distinguished fore-fathers to chaste wombs. Whenever a predecessor from among them died the follower stood up for the cause of the religion of Allāh.
ai.seo_question: How does the text describe the lineage and succession of the Prophets?
ai.summary: This passage from Nahj al-Balagha articulates the concept of *Tanasukh* (succession) within the pure lineage of the Prophets, emphasizing their divine preservation in noble lineages and pure wombs. It underscores the continuity of divine guidance, where each Prophet succeeds the previous one to uphold God's religion, a theme central to Shia understanding of prophetic succession and the unbroken chain of revelation.
